'''C1''' is the fifth level of the [[CEFR The Common European Framework of Reference for Languages|Common European Framework]] and the lower '''Proficient User''' level. Its informal name is '''Effective Operational Proficiency'''.

== What C1 actually means ==

A C1 speaker can understand a wide range of demanding, longer texts and '''recognise implicit meaning'''. They can express themselves fluently and spontaneously '''without much obvious searching for expressions'''. They can use the language '''flexibly and effectively for social, academic and professional purposes''', and produce clear, well-structured, detailed text on complex subjects, showing controlled use of organisational patterns, connectors and cohesive devices.

Two things separate C1 from [[CEFR Level B2|B2]], and neither is vocabulary size:

* '''Implicit meaning.''' Irony, understatement, register shifts, what is being avoided. A B2 speaker understands what was said; a C1 speaker understands what was meant.
* '''Structure.''' At C1 a person can organise an extended argument in the language, not merely express its parts.

== What it is worth in practice ==

* '''University.''' The usual requirement for '''postgraduate study''', and for undergraduate study at selective institutions.
* '''Work.''' The level for senior professional roles conducted in the language — leading meetings, negotiating, writing for publication, representing an organisation.
* '''Teaching.''' A C1 learner is the best-paid segment of the language-teaching market, and teaching them is a different professional activity from teaching beginners. What they usually want is not more general language but a '''register''' — see [[Language Registers Business Religious and Trade Language]].

== Certificates at C1 with staying power ==

* '''English''' — '''C1 Advanced''' (the Certificate in Advanced English), '''introduced in 1991''' and set at C1 from the outset. It was designed into the level rather than retrofitted to it, which is unusual.
* '''Spanish''' — '''DELE C1''', Instituto Cervantes.
* '''French''' — '''DALF C1''', awarded in the name of the French Ministry of Education. The DALF series begins here; it is a lifetime diploma and is accepted by French universities in place of a separate entrance language test.
* '''German''' — '''Goethe-Zertifikat C1''', Goethe-Institut.
* '''Italian''' — '''CILS Tre C1''', '''CELI 4''', '''PLIDA C1'''.

== How long it takes ==

Commonly cited estimates run to '''700 to 800 guided hours''' or more for a closely related language, and considerably more for a distant one. Most learners who reach C1 do so through sustained use — work, study, residence — rather than through classes alone.

== Where to go next ==

[[CEFR Level C2]], which is the top of the scale and is frequently misunderstood.
